recognize_zh: CellaVision 截圖中的每顆細胞都是比紅血球大 1.5–2 倍的母細胞：核質比極高、染色質細緻均勻、細胞質只剩一小片淡藍色且無顆粒，許多細胞可見小圓空泡與手鏡狀（hand-mirror）細胞質突起；形態一致符合淋巴母細胞，此例為兒童 B-ALL。
features: Monotonous population of blasts about 1.5-2 times red cell diameter
Very high N:C ratio with scant pale blue agranular cytoplasm, often as a polar tail or bleb (hand-mirror forms)
Round to irregular or angular nuclei with fine, homogeneous chromatin; nucleoli inconspicuous
Small discrete clear vacuoles in many cells
No Auer rods or granules; background red cells unremarkable with rare platelets
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear, digitally captured cell gallery (CellaVision), shows a monotonous population of circulating blasts. The blasts are small to intermediate, measuring about 1.5 to 2 times the diameter of a red cell, with very high N:C ratio, round to irregular nuclei, finely dispersed homogeneous chromatin, and inconspicuous nucleoli. The cytoplasm is scant, pale blue, and agranular, frequently drawn out into a polar tail or bleb, and several cells contain small discrete clear vacuoles; Auer rods are absent. Findings are consistent with lymphoblasts and, together with the flow cytometric phenotype, support B-lymphoblastic leukemia.

ddx.vs: Myeloblasts are generally larger with more cytoplasm, prominent nucleoli, and may contain granules or Auer rods; flow cytometry is required when blasts are agranular.
Burkitt cells have deeply basophilic cytoplasm with numerous prominent vacuoles and more clumped chromatin with multiple nucleoli, and are TdT-negative mature B cells.
Reactive lymphocytes have abundant cytoplasm that scallops around red cells and more condensed chromatin, with a heterogeneous rather than monotonous population.
Hematogones are rare in peripheral blood, have more homogeneous smudged dark chromatin, and show an orderly maturation pattern on flow cytometry.
